text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 5

The panel's composition can't explain your outcome: the person hired was also a woman, so sex didn't separate you two. An all-women panel in a field like economics is unusual, but unusual isn't improper — and raising it would read as insinuation without a mechanism, damaging your credibility on the point that actually matters.

Your real grievance is procedural: you're more qualified on the stated academic criteria, yet "industry experience" appears to have been weighted in a way that may not match the advertised requirements. And you're owed a written explanation.

Send a firm follow-up citing the deadline under your university's rules or national administrative law, requesting the criteria, scoring and panel minutes.
